item.title: What Modern Betting Infrastructure Means for the Future of the UK Leisure Economy
item.description: The evolution of betting is undeniable. Whether it’s sports or the most common casino games, it’s clear there has been a very big shift when it comes to how individuals enjoy betting. Read more: What Modern Betting Infrastructure Means for the Future of the UK Leisure Economy

item.title: Mark Dixon: ‘Banning working from home is idiotic’
item.description: In an interview with The Times, IWG founder Mark Dixon defends hybrid working, criticises calls to ban WFH and reflects on Regus, WeWork and a possible US listing. Read more: Mark Dixon: ‘Banning working from home is idiotic’

item.title: Greene King considers job cuts as soaring costs squeeze pub sector
item.description: Greene King is reviewing up to 100 head office roles as Britain’s second-largest pub operator battles rising taxes, labour costs and weakening consumer demand. Read more: Greene King considers job cuts as soaring costs squeeze pub sector

item.title: Alphabet ramps up AI spending with up to $185bn capital plan
item.description: Alphabet plans to spend up to $185bn this year as it accelerates AI investment, reporting strong fourth-quarter results but facing investor scrutiny over soaring costs. Read more: Alphabet ramps up AI spending with up to $185bn capital plan

item.title: Gender pay gap won’t close until 2056 at current pace, warns TUC
item.description: The TUC warns the UK gender pay gap, currently 12.8%, will not close for another 30 years without faster reform, with finance showing the widest disparity. Read more: Gender pay gap won’t close until 2056 at current pace, warns TUC

item.title: Workers’ rights reforms prompt a third of employers to curb hiring
item.description: A CIPD survey finds 37% of employers plan to cut permanent hiring due to the Employment Rights Act, with more than half expecting increased workplace disputes. Read more: Workers’ rights reforms prompt a third of employers to curb hiring
